resources.string: Location access is off. You can browse and edit your journal, but new routes and automatic visits need location access.
Location was not allowed. Recording has not started. You can keep using your existing journal.
Approximate location is on. Routes may have gaps or no saved points, and visits may be missed. Precise location is optional.
Notifications are off. Recording can continue, but Android may hide its status notification. Open Whereday to check or stop recording.
Whereday uses location to save route points and detect visits while recording. You can browse and edit existing history without allowing location.
If Android no longer shows a request, change access in app settings. Returning from settings does not start recording.
The permission request could not open. Try again, or use app settings.
App settings could not open. In Android Settings, find Whereday under Apps and review its permissions.
